newsitem.title: UK: BT price cuts fail to impress UK watchdog.
newsitem.headline: BT price cuts fail to impress UK watchdog.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc on Wednesday cut the prices for calls to two mobile telephone companies but its industry regulator, Oftel, remained unimpressed.
"It looks as if prices are still too high," said an Oftel spokeswoman. Oftel's director general, Don Cruickshank, is still investigating price levels which he believes should fall significantly.
BT said it would trim prices from its fixed line network to mobile market leader Vodafone Group Plc and BT's majority-owned Cellnet company from August 7.

Daytime call prices will be cut by one pence to 36.5 pence (61 cents) per minute and weekend calls by two pence to 10.5p per minute. The sharpest price cut is for evening and night time calls, which will come down by three pence to 22p per minute.
Calls are charged by the second, with a minimun charge of five pence, BT noted in a statement.
It is cheaper to call the other two, purely digital mobile operators -- Orange Plc and One2One -- from BT telephones. BT said those charges would also continue to be reduced but gave no details.
"We look forward to more reductions in the coming months," Keith Carrington, BT's pricing manager, said in a statement.
Regulator Cruickshank has mainly blamed mobile telephone companies for charging too much for delivering calls from fixed networks to their own customers.
About two-thirds of the retail price of calls to Vodafone's and Cellnet's networks goes to those two operators and BT keeps the rest.
Oftel is looking for the prices that BT pays the mobile companies for delivering calls -- an average of 19.66p per minute before Wednesday's price cuts -- to fall to 10-14p per minute.
The watchdog, which has called for mobile firms to negotiate lower interconnection charges with each other, plans a statement in due course.
